No building is depicted in direct adjacency to pole locations based on the plan geometry and scale.
agentTrace.reasoning: Reviewer Convention requires new buildings to maintain clearance from existing streetlight poles. Review of the site layout confirms all proposed buildings are set back substantially from property boundaries where poles are located, creating adequate separation distance. The buildings appear to be far enough from the existing poles that no clearance violation is present.

applicableAreas: All proposed buildings relative to existing utility poles

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 4 (existing survey) legend indicates that down guy wires from utility poles are depicted with 'GUY' notation. Vision analysis of Sheet 4 confirmed that guy wires are marked on poles at property corners. Sheet 9 (site plan) shows driveways, accessible pathways, and parking areas, but does not include dimension annotations showing the location of guy anchor points or guy wire alignments relative to proposed accessible routes and driveways. The Electric Notes on Sheet 3, Block 19 require the owner to include tree pruning and removal work within construction limits, but do not specifically address guy wire relocation or conflicts.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) and practical utility design distinguish down guy wires (distribution support cables) from angled guy wires (transmission tower guys). Down guy anchors from existing poles can conflict with proposed accessible paths and driveways. While guy wires are shown on the existing survey, their specific locations and potential conflicts with proposed site features are not documented on the proposed site plan with dimension callouts or relocation/resolution notes.

applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations relative to proposed accessible routes and driveways
findings.comment: Site plan must clearly identify existing down guy wire anchor locations and document resolution of any conflicts with proposed accessible routes and driveways through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting poles, or provide plan notes confirming no conflicts exist.

agentTrace.observation: Review of sheet index and facts.md shows no transmission facilities on this site. No transmission structures or transmission towers with angled guy wire systems are depicted on any plans. The utility poles on the property appear to be distribution-scale poles based on the existing survey depiction.
agentTrace.reasoning: EL-1.41 applies only to angled guy easements from transmission structures (high-voltage facilities). No transmission facilities or transmission towers are shown on this project, therefore this requirement does not apply.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 4 (existing survey) depicts utility poles at property corners with guy notations indicating down guy support cables. However, no easement exhibit or legal description of down guy anchor easements is provided on the site plan sheets. Sheets 2 (Plat) and the easement exhibits focus on drainage, wastewater, public utility, and electric easements, but down guy anchor easements are not separately depicted or dimensioned.
agentTrace.reasoning: Reviewer Convention requires down guy anchor points to have dedicated 10-foot-wide easements extending minimum 5 feet past where the guy enters ground. While down guys exist on the property (shown on existing survey), the specific easement boundaries for these down guys are not depicted on the plat or easement exhibit. Without documented easement areas on the plat, compliance with the easement dedication requirement cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points at property corners
findings.comment: Easement exhibit and plat must identify and show 10-foot-wide down guy anchor easements extending minimum 5 feet past ground entry point for each down guy support cable on property.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed pole-mounted transformers at multiple locations on the site serving the electrical distribution to buildings. However, no surveyed elevation or height data is provided for these transformers, and no section views showing vertical clearance from existing overhead electric lines to the tops of the transformer equipment are documented on any sheet.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformers to maintain 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric lines when lines are above or adjacent to transformer locations. While transformers are shown on the plan, the specific type (pole-mounted vs. pad-mounted) and vertical clearance dimensions are not documented. Without surveyed transformer elevation data and clearance dimensions on section views, compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Proposed transformer locations if located beneath overhead lines
findings.comment: Electrical design plan must specify transformer types (pole-mounted or pad-mounted) and provide section views with dimension annotations showing vertical clearance from overhead line conductors to top of transformer equipment, verifying 7.5-foot minimum clearance.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electrical infrastructure with transformers and service points. No niche service configurations (covered or recessed installations with structures, canopies, or covered areas above equipment) are depicted on the site plan or electrical design sheets. All proposed electrical equipment appears to be exposed/open installation types.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 applies only to transformers or switchgears in niche service configurations (covered or recessed installations). No niche-configured electrical equipment is shown in the proposed design, therefore this requirement does not apply.

agentTrace.observation: Sheets 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) and 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) show construction staging and phasing. However, no explicit construction logistics plan, site logistics diagram, or notes on Sheets 5, 8, or 6 (Erosion Control Notes) document the location of construction staging areas, equipment laydown zones, crane swing radius zones, or work platforms relative to the existing overhead electric lines. The distance between construction activity areas and overhead lines is not dimensioned or noted.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 requires construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms to maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA. This is a temporary requirement distinct from permanent clearances. While construction is planned on the site with overhead utilities present, the specific construction staging layout and documented 10-foot clearances from overhead lines are not provided on the submitted plans.

applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, work platforms
findings.comment: Construction logistics plan or site phasing plan must document staging area boundaries, crane swing radius zones, equipment laydown areas, and work platforms with dimension annotations verifying 10-foot radial clearance from all overhead electric lines. Construction management notes must address overhead line safety during all phases.

agentTrace.observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 3 (General Notes) - all block content; Sheet 6 (Erosion Control Notes); cover sheet notes; and the Electric Notes on Sheet 3, Block 19 reveals that the site plan includes Electric Notes acknowledging Austin Energy requirements and stating 'The owner of the property is responsible for maintaining clearances required by the National Electric Safety Code, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations...' However, there is NO note on the cover sheet or general notes stating: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' or any reference to Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 requires a note stating owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines, per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. The Electric Notes reference OSHA and NESC clearance requirements but do not include the specific 48-hour notification requirement for high-voltage work. This is a documentation deficiency - the required note is missing from the plans.

applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes
findings.comment: Add note to cover sheet or general notes: 'Owner/contractor shall notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any construction activities or operations near overhead electric lines. Contact Austin Energy at [number] per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed electrical service infrastructure, but no service-mast through-roof installations are depicted on the site plan or on any building elevation sheets. The design appears to utilize underground service distribution from transformers on pad/pole to individual building service points.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 applies only to service-mast through-roof installations where the mast penetrates the roof to connect service lines. No service masts are shown on the submitted plans; the design uses underground service routing, therefore this requirement does not apply.
